text: A Gromark key is a stream of digits. Each known letter under its carved letter tells the shift used there; a shift of 10 or more cannot be a single digit, so it needs a bigger number base.
Over all 10,404 pairs of tables built from K1 to K3 words, the smallest base any pair allows is 17; ten shuffled coppers give 17 to 19.
No pair allows base 15 or less, so the ordinary base-10 Gromark is out on every one of these tables.
